newsitem.title: USA: US financial services stocks rise amid merger news.
newsitem.headline: US financial services stocks rise amid merger news.

text.p: Financial services stocks were mostly higher on Wednesday after a proposed merger between Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter, Discover & Co fueled speculation of further consolidation in the industry.
The merger could jumpstart a new consolidation rush on Wall Street, with regional retail brokerage firms being among the most attractive takeover candidates, analysts and traders said.

"These companies have grown faster than other financial services companies," said James Inglis, an analyst with Philo Smith & Co. "They have outperformed others in the sector and they will likely continue to do that."
Alex. Brown Inc gained 2-1/2 to 55, A.G. Edwards Inc jumped 2-1/8 to 36-5/8, EVEREN Capital Corp increased 3/8 to 24 and Legg Mason Inc gained 1-5/8 to 47-1/4.
PaineWebber Group Inc, however, bucked the trend. The brokerage firm's stock had rallied recently amid market rumors that it could be an imminent takeover target.
Wall Street had speculated that Morgan Stanley or BankAmerica Corp could be possible suitors.
PaineWebber dropped 3-3/8 to 35-1/2 after Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter announced their proposed stock-swap merger.
"There may be a little bit of a letdown involved in that situation," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal and Co.

Among other brokerage shares, Salomon Inc gained 1-1/4 to 56-3/4, Bear Stearns Cos Inc jumped 1-1/2 to 33-3/8 and Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc added 1-3/8 to 35-1/4. Merrill Lynch and Co Inc increased 1-3/4 to 87-1/8.
Travelers Group Inc, which owns Smith Barney, shed 1/8 to 54-3/8.
